clue.text: Heavy fall of feathers on stream

blocks.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
to stream is to pour

explanation.surface: Feathers drifting down onto a stream in a heavy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a sudden heavy shower of rain, a heavy fall from the sky.

clue.text: Cartographers look for capital

blocks.note: the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapmakers
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Mapmakers searching for a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The OS (Ordnance Survey) is the British government's mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Auntie holds duck by carnivore

indicators.note: something that holds another item has it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Auntie is the affectionate nickname for the BBC
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
at and by both mean beside or near

explanation.surface: An aunt holding a duck beside some meat-eating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation) is nicknamed Auntie; O goes inside after the first B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobcat is a North American wild cat, a meat-eating predator.

clue.text: Conserve rubbish?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to conserve is to consume a smaller amount
second meaning: worthless, no good

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition only works split into two words, USE LESS; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless or hopeless is useless; to conserve resources means to consume less of them.

clue.text: Lady goes back in before receivers

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read backwards
placed in something means set within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal
a woman's name standing for any lady

explanation.surface: A woman heading back inside ahead of some radio receivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are aerials that pick up radio or TV signals, devices that receive.

clue.text: Revert to mountain road?

blocks.note: first meaning, as two words: to change back
second meaning: a road zigzagging up a steep slope

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the phrase 'switch back', the second the single word for a hairpin road.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a zigzag road climbing a mountainside; to switch back is to return to a previous state.

clue.text: Daughter found beneath a non-English fruit tree

indicators.note: non-English means the English abbreviation is taken out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
a citrus fruit
standard abbreviation, removed here
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter discovered sheltering under a foreign fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue D 'found beneath' the rest goes at the bottom; 'fruit' looks like part of the definition but supplies the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is a tree of the rose family grown for its edible nuts.

clue.text: Cousin in takeaway repeatedly for food

indicators.note: read as 'take away', it tells you to remove some letters from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters removed

explanation.surface: A cousin eating a takeaway again and again for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takeaway' looks like a meal, but read as take away it removes IN from COUSIN; 'repeatedly' says the remainder appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina grains.

clue.text: Column more recently changed direction

indicators.note: changing direction swaps right for left, so one letter is exchanged for another

blocks.note: newer means more recent

explanation.surface: A column that has lately been turned to face another way.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the end of NEWER becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the central post of a spiral staircase or the post at the foot of a banister.

clue.text: Release from run-down accommodation

indicators.note: accommodation is housing, so the phrase houses the letters inside it

blocks.note: sits inside these letters, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Being let out of shabby lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to loosen or release it.

clue.text: Notice difference after college gathering

indicators.note: making a difference to the word changes it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for college
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Noticing how things differ after leaving college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after college' puts COLL in front of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection is a group of things gathered together, a gathering.

clue.text: Spoil Tesco''s produce

indicators.note: produce as a verb means make up or fashion, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables at Tesco going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a noun for fresh food, but it is the anagram signal; Tesco is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or indulge someone, as you spoil a child.

clue.text: Large vessel holds course

blocks.note: surface reading: a big ship keeps to its route at sea
setter's reading: a big serving dish containing the first course of a meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'course' both suggest sailing; at the dinner table they mean a dish and part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This lidded bowl is brought to table holding the soup served as a starter.

clue.text: Son has nude frolic with parasol

indicators.note: to frolic is to romp about, so the letters jump around into a new order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for son
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A boy enjoying a naked romp, holding a parasol.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella giving shade from the sun, which is a sunshade.

clue.text: Rejoice! Time to drink one in pub

indicators.note: one thing put in another sits inside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for time
a spirit
the Roman numeral for one
PH, public house, is a map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A cry of joy: it's time to go for a drink in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside RUM after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to exult in victory, to celebrate with great joy.

clue.text: Father popular with bird (peacock)

blocks.note: an informal word for father
in fashion, popular
a noisy bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Dad is popular with a bird, perhaps a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: '(peacock)' looks like a gloss on 'bird' but is the definition, in its sense of a vain showy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, conceited person who struts about like a peacock.

clue.text: Fine author, a long time unknown

blocks.note: a pen writes, standing for the writer
taken as written
standard abbreviation for long
standard abbreviation for time
in algebra x, y and z are the unknowns

explanation.surface: A fine writer who has long been neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise for the author, but it is the noun for a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a penalty, a sum paid as punishment.

clue.text: Brother to net soft winner

blocks.note: to net something is to trap it
p (piano) means soft in music
the winner comes 1st, with 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A brother out to catch an easy winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a monk of a strict Cistercian order, and monks are called brothers.

clue.text: An acknowledgment — it''s right to hold up work

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within others
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for right
a piece of art or music is a work
the setter takes only the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: An admission that it is fine to delay the work.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: R and the T of 'it' hold the reversed work, but nothing signals taking only T from 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written note confirming that money or goods have been received.

clue.text: Many think about bonus note

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to mull over is to think
a tip is an extra payment
one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Plenty of people pondering a note about a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple means numerous, several, more than one.

clue.text: Uncle returns somewhat poorer usually

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so the letters come from inside the phrase
something that returns comes back the way it went, so read it backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: An uncle tends to come back somewhat poorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, a moneylender.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at high interest, like a pawnbroker, nicknamed uncle.

clue.text: Harsh decree issued when fool comes back with cheap goods

indicators.note: coming back is going the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: to kid is to fool someone
tat is cheap, tasteless stuff

explanation.surface: A tough order issued when a joker returns with junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is an order imposed by a ruler without consent, a harsh decree.

clue.text: Trickle produced by drunk man standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
any man's name will do; Sid is a common one

explanation.surface: A trickle coming from a drunk who is still on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil can mean to let fall in drops, so it is a synonym of trickle.

clue.text: Promises to return a month before king reformed Senate

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters are read backwards
something reformed is remade in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
R for rex, Latin for king
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pledge to come back in a month, before the king shakes up the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarantees are formal assurances or pledges, so they are promises.

clue.text: Feel depressed when vehicle isn''t finished

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a small motorbike

explanation.surface: Feeling low because the car isn't ready yet.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and gloomy, which is to feel depressed.

clue.text: Mother has hands for clay

blocks.note: informal word for mother
the two hands, right and left, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Mum gets her hands into some clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marl is a crumbly soil of clay mixed with lime, used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Opponent cut short by one behind purge

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: an enemy opposes you
a means one, as in a book

explanation.surface: A rival beaten by someone behind him in a purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places A after the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes out the bowel, a purge of the body.

clue.text: Sister to petition about ten reformers initially

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the others
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: to press is to urge or petition
10 written as the letters I and O
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A nun lobbying for ten reformers.
explanation.definitionFit: A prioress is the nun in charge of a priory, a senior religious sister.
